page: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v6 is a compute-focused instance within Azure's D-family lineup, built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon 8573C processors. The virtual machine provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled, supported by a 4.2 GHz clock speed and a 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 64 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. In addition to standard managed disk compatibility, the instance includes 1890 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Acceleration hardware includes Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions, while discrete GPU hardware is omitted.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong capabilities in both raw instruction throughput and data manipulation. The instance scores high in Geekbench single-core (2024.0) and multi-core (17402.0) metrics, supported by top-decile image processing results and robust large-block uncached memory read bandwidth exceeding 211 GB/sec. Multithreaded decompression through bzip3 reaches 203.81 GB/sec, and web serving throughput delivers 54.77 GB/sec. Small-model LLM execution shows high efficiency, generating 396.8 tokens per second on 135M parameter models using AMX acceleration. However, processing larger language models highlights throughput limitations, with 70B parameter models falling to 2.77 tokens per second due to memory density ceilings.

The 2.0 GB per vCPU configuration offers cost-efficient compute density for organizations running CPU-bound services that do not require high RAM footprints. The integrated 1890 GB NVMe volume delivers fast scratch disk IO without requiring separate provisioned storage volumes. Primary tradeoffs stem from the lower memory-to-core ratio and the absence of bundled public IPv4 addresses. Microsoft Azure D32lds_v6 is well aligned with workloads such as web serving tiers, multi-threaded batch compression, continuous integration build jobs, image processing pipelines, and localized data processing applications.
description: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v6 is an x86_64 compute-dense virtual machine powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor. It offers 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 64 GB of RAM, and a bundled 1890 GB local NVMe SSD. Featuring Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction extensions without a discrete GPU, the system achieves strong performance in Geekbench compute tasks, multithreaded data decompression, static web serving, and small-parameter AI inference. Its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides an efficient hardware footprint for compute-dominated environments, though the lower memory allocation limits very large parameter models. The integrated high-capacity NVMe drive provides immediate local throughput for scratch storage and caching. Microsoft Azure D32lds_v6 is well suited for high-concurrency web serving, media processing, compilation workloads, and compute-focused batch processing pipelines.
